cards.back: Key movements: Bauhaus (form follows function, industrial production), Art Deco (geometric, luxurious), Memphis (playful, postmodern), De Stijl (abstract, primary colours).

cards.back: Form follows function means the shape of an object should relate to its purpose — but this principle has been both followed and deliberately challenged.

cards.front: What should you know about three-dimensional design exam tips?
cards.back: Name SPECIFIC designers, objects and buildings. Explain CONTEXT — what was happening in society. Analyse the FORM-FUNCTION relationship. Show how the movement's philosophy influences YOUR design choices, not just their visual style.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Design movements are just art history — they have nothing to do with making products or spaces. Correct: Design movements directly shaped how things are made and used. Bauhaus created the template for modern industrial design. Art Deco influenced architecture and consumer products.
